full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: Both these two Rules relate to the judicial custody of Shilpi Rani Sarker, daughter of Sree Tarapada Sarker and arises out of the same case, Nari-O-Shishu Case No. 35 of 1996 pending in the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Special Judge Adalat, Rajbari. 

 2. The Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1043 of 1997 was at the instance of Sree Tarapada Sarker and the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1157 of 1997 was at the instance of Shilpi Rani Sarker, at present Shireen Akhter, wife of Syeed Mondal alias Sayedur Rahman MondaI. At the time of issuance of Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1157 of 1997 it was ordered that the Rule would be heard along with the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1043 of 1997. 

 3. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of these two Rules are that, Sree Tarapada Sarker as informant lodged a written Ejahar on 10-8-96 with Rajbari Sadar Police Station mentioning Provisions of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Special Provision) Act, 1995 to the effect that Shilpi Rani Sarker is his college going (HSC examinee) daughter and on 7-8-96 accused Abu Sayeed Mondal with the help of other two accused persons, namely, (1) Jiban Kumar Pramanik and (2) Abdul Gafur Mondal, enticed away his daughter Shilpi Rani Sarkar to compel her to marry him against her will or to compel her to have sexual intercourse causing mental and physical torture upon her or handed her over to the women traffickers in exchange of money. The police investigated the case and submitted charge-sheet against the accused-persons on 7-11-96 under sections 9(Kha) and (Ga) and 14 of said Act. The case was sent to the learned Special Judge, Nuri-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Special Court at Rajbari on 24-11-96 and the learned Court has taken cognisance of the offence against the accused persons. Thereafter on 15-1-97 the accused Sayeed Mondal and said Shilpa Rani Sarker naming herself as Shireen Akhter surrendered before the Court and both of them prayed for bail. Their prayers were rejected. Shilpi Rani Sarkar was sent to judicial custody and accused Sayeed MondaI was sent to jail. Thereafter on 2-2-97 Sree Tarapada Sarker moved a petition for taking the victim girl under his custody claiming the victim to be a minor. The prayer was rejected on 2-2-97 by the learned Judge in Nari-O-Shishu case No. 35 of 1996 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Special Judge Adalat, Rajbari. Hence, Sree Tarapada Sarker moved this Court under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 4. Shilpi Rani Sarkar at present Shireen Akhter moved this Court under section 491 CrPC challenging the order for keeping her under judicial custody on the ground, amongst others, that she is not an accused in the case and she is sui-juris and has voluntarily married Syed Mondal after embracing Islam of her own will and, as such, keeping her under judicial custody against her will is illegal and obtained the Rule. 

 6. For determination of the above it is to be seen whether the victim girl Shilpi Rani Sarker alias Shireen Akhter is a minor or not and for that matter determination of her age is a vital issue. It appears from the supplementary affidavit filed by Sree Tarapada Sarker in Miscellaneous Case No. 1043 of 1997 that the date of birth of Shilpi Rani Sarker according to her SSC Examination certificate is 8th June, 1979 copy of which has been annexed as Annexure, whereas the victim girl claims her date of birth to be 1-9-77 on the basis of a certificate issued by her primary school, copy of which has been annexed with the application as Annexure. 

 7. Mr. SN Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Sree Tarapada Sarker, submits that the victim girl is under the age of 18 years and, as such, she is minor and accordingly, Sree Tarapada Sarker being her father is entitled to get her custody. The learned Advocate referred to the case of Khairunnessa vs. Illy Begum and another, reported in 1996 BLT (AD) 112 and in 48 DLR (AD) 67 in support of his submission that the statement of victim girl should not be taken to be conclusive as to determination of her age. In the said decision it has been observed that the High Court Division, it appears, put much reliance on the physical appearance which may not always provide a correct guide for ascertaining the age of a girl child who is growing up. In some cases physical development may take place which may be regarded as precocious while in some other cases there may not be as such development as is natural with the passage of time. In any event having regard to the fact in this particular case that all the available materials so far, supported the claim of the mother that the girl was aged about 15/16 years except the statement of the girl herself, the High Court Division cannot be said to have acted judiciously and properly in ignoring the said materials and relying solely on the statement of the girl herself and their own observation of the girl and in making a finding thereupon that she was a major above 18 years. We are of the opinion that the mother has a reasonable grievance to make against the impugned judgment which does not seem to have been passed upon a proper appreciation keeping in view the welfare of the girl who is alleged to be a minor." We are in respectful agreement with the decision but we do not find any relevance of the said decision in deciding the issue involved in this case, since in the present case according to Sree Tarapada Sarker the date of birth of her daughter is 8-6-79 and hence she was over 16 years of age even on the date of occurrence on 7-8-96. From the contents of the applications upon which the Rules were issued, it appears both the petitioners admit that Shilpi Rani Sarker is aged over 16 years. The learned Advocate then referred to another decision of our Appellate Division in the case of Sree Mongal Chandra Nandi vs. Bangladesh reported in 1997 BLT (AD) 1, wherein dealing with the custody of minor girl their Lordships have held that the learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record found the victim girl, Dhali Rani Nandi, to be a minor. It is not disputed before us that under the law the father is the lawful guardian of her minor daughter. The learned Judges having found the victim girl to be minor ought to have given the minor in the lawful custody of the father. The opinion of the minor is irrelevant and the same cannot be a condition precedent for giving her custody to the father. The learned Judges failed to consider that a minor's refusal to go with her father is not at all a material consideration regarding her custody. Father being the best well-wisher of a minor daughter is entitled to custody and in her own interest she should be given in her father's custody. Further, the minor girl is an unfortunate victim of an offence of an abduction and it is not understood why she should be detained till the disposal of the criminal case as well as till she attains the age of 18 years. It is not desirable that she should be kept in jail for a long and indefinite period which will be detrimental to her welfare. In that view of the matter, the learned Judges of the High Court Division ought to have given the custody of the minor girl to the appellant." We are in full agreement with decision of their Lorships, however the said decision is not relevant for our purpose inasmuch as in the said decision the victim girl was found to be a minor, which is not in the present case. The learned Advocate could not satisfy us with any materials except referring to section 366A of the Penal Code that Shilpi Rani Sarkar is a minor. 

 9. Relying on the aforesaid sections the learned Advocate for the victim girl submits that the allegations made in the First Information Report do not attract the ingredients of the aforesaid sections inasmuch as the victim girl was neither abducted nor kidnapped and or taken away against her will or compelled her to marry against her will or forced to or seduced her to illicit sexual intercourse. In support of his contention he took us through the certified copy of the written statement, prepared in her own handwriting, submitted in the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Adalat, Rajbari, in Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 3 of 1996 on 15-1-97, which has been annexed as Annexure-C to application of Criminal Misc. Case No.1157 of 1997 wherein she has stated that she is sui-jurisand embraced Islam voluntarily and also married Sayeed Mondal of her own will by a registered Kabinnama and she was pregnant and that Sayeed Mondal did not abduct or kidnap her as alleged and she wants to go with her husband. The learned Advocate submitted that while Shilpi Rani Sarkar was under judicial custody for about 3-V, months having no influence of the accused persons she was produced before this Hon'ble Court on 30-4-97 and she gave a statement to the effect that she embraced Islam and married Sayeed Mondal alias Sayedur Rahman and she is pregnant and wants to go with her husband and that she is not a minor. Relying on said statement the learned Advocate submitted that there should not be any doubt that the accused Sayeed Mondal did not commit any offence as alleged and that the victim girl was neither kidnapped or abducted nor enticed away against her will and that she not being an accused in the case and since she is above 16 years of age she cannot be kept under judicial custody any further against her will and is entitled to stay with anyone according to her wish. He further submits that sections 361, 366 and 366A of the Penal Code are not attracted in this case inasmuch as the ingredients of those sections require that the victim girl ought to be abducted for the purpose of marrying against her will or illicit sexual intercourse by another man. But in the present case accused Syed Mondal has, in fact, married Shilpi Rani Sarker after her conversion as a Muslim and she went with Sayeed Mondal on her own will. He further submits that the age of 18 years mentioned in section 366A of the Penal Code is for the purpose of attracting the offence punishable under the said section and not for the purpose of determining age relating to minority. In support of his submissions he referred to the decision reported in 35 DLR 315 in the case of Ananda Mohan Banerjee vs. Slate, wherein their Lordships held that the victim girl who is above the age of 16 years as of today cannot be detained in custody against her will, as such, the petitioner Ananda Mohan Banerjee is not entitled to the custody of the victim girl as prayed for by him in the Rule and the victim girl is free to go wherever she likes. The Rule is accordingly discharged". Facts of the said case is similar to the present case in that Ananda Mohan Banerjee lodged First Information Report to the effect that his minor girl Preti Banerjee was kidnapped from their custody by accused Delwar Hossain, Police arrested both victim girl and the accused. Then said Ananda Mohan prayed for her custody in the Rule. In deciding the said case their Lordships relied on the case of Jahanara Begum alias Jotsna Rani Saha vs. State and another, reported in 15 DLR 148, wherein their Lordships held that "where a person is brought before the court is aged 16 years or over, the will of such person, when the question before the Court is whether she or he should be detained or allowed to go from court's custody, must be allowed to prevail. The position of such a persons is, at the most, that of a witness and therefore not being an accused she or he cannot be detained against her or his will." In the said case the victim girl was alleged to be 14 years of age. The court however found that she was on the admission of her father himself more than 16 years and therefore held that it would not be just to keep the girl in custody against her will. Their Lordships in deciding the case reported in 35 DLR 315 also referred to the case of Jesmin Sultana alias Manika Rani vs. State and another decided by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Revision No. 522 of 1997, in which case it was held that "as the girl was above 16 years of age as of today, the Court did not see any reason to keep her in judicial custody against her will, particularly when she was neither an accused nor has been cited as a witness in the First Information Report" The learned Advocate on the point of judicial custody referred to the case reported in 15 DLR 148 wherein their Lordships have held that "the judicial custody for a temporary period is required to give a chance to the victim girl to develop her own independent opinion, free from external pressures". Their Lordship further observed therein that "the very nature of the duties cast on courts carries with it the widest discretionary powers in the exercise of control over the conduct of the proceedings before them. This view is now well established and enshrined in a number of decisions by eminent Judges of the Superior Courts of this Sub-continent. Indeed, it was necessary to recognise this Rule for ensuring the real and substantial justice between the contending parties seeking justice in Courts whether Civil or Criminal. Taking a minor into custody or arranging for his or her detention, with a view to temporarily isolating him or her from certain influences, may be necessitated by the dictates of justice. That custody or detention is certainly different from the custody of an alleged criminal and even of a political detenu. It has the complexion of the custody of a guardian. It has an objective difference from confinement or placing restriction on his or her movement. This is a discretion inherent in the Court." 

 11. In the present case it is found from the materials on record that the victim girl Shilpi Rani Sarker alias Shireen Akhter is aged above 16 years and she is not an accused in this case. Having regard to the SSC certificate produced by the father of the victim girl, wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 8-6-79, it appears that she is around 18 years now. In the premises, in view of decisions of our court in the case reported in 35 DLR 315 and the cases referred to therein and our discussion made above, we do not find any reason to deliver custody of the victim girl Shilpi Rani Sarker now Shireen Akhter to her father Sree Tarapada Sarker as prayed for inasmuch as the judicial custody of Shilpi Rani Sarker in the facts and circumstances of the case is not lawful and therefore the victim girl is to be set at free allowing her to live with any one according to her will and choice. In this connection we may also refer to the decision in the case of Fatema Begum @ urmile Rani vs. Gogeswar Nath reported in 9 BID (11C) 469, wherein referring to section 552 CrPC it has been held that the petitioner being above the age of 16 years cannot be handed over to her father or to anybody even by Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate but to be set at liberty." In this decision the case reported in 35 DLR 315 was also considered that their Lordships relied thereon. The facts of the present case and that of the case out of which the case reported in 9 BLD arose are similar. 

 12. Accordingly, the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1043 of 1997 is discharged. The Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1157 of 1997 is made absolute. The keeping of Shilpi Rani Sarkar now Shireen Akhter under judicial custody against her will is not lawful and Sree Tarapada Sarker is not entitled to the custody of Shilpi Rani Sarker, who is free to go wherever she likes. The order dated 2-2-97 passed in Nari-O-Shishu case No.35 of 1996 by the learned Special Judge Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Adalat, Rajbari, so far it relates to the judicial custody of Shilpi Rani Sarkar daughter of Sree Tarapada Sarker, is set aside.
